newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian river polluted by possible eruption.
newsitem.headline: Colombian river polluted by possible eruption.

text.p: Thousands of fish and several cows died after tonnes of mud washed down a river in an isolated region of northwest Colombia following a possible volcanic eruption, geologists said on Wednesday.

Thick deposits of clay and soil began appearing in the San Jorge River late on Tuesday, but experts said it was difficult to determine the exact cause given the remote nature of the area in a mountainous corner of Cordoba province known as El Nudo de Paramillo.
A spokeswoman at the Bogota-based National Disaster Centre said a team of observers were due to fly over the area later on Wednesday to see if they could spot signs of a volaco erupting.

"This has caused the death of millions of fish and some cattle. We presume this is caused by the eruption of a volcano or a landslide in the mountains," Alvaro Vidal, head of the Cordoba Disaster Office told the Noticiero Nacional TV news programme.
A spokesman for the National Geological Institute (INGEOMINAS) said the volcano was what is termed locally a "mud-volcano," which spews out boiling mud instead of rocks and molten lava.
